questions.question: Which of the following recommends Minimum Support Prices for crops in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices**__

 __
 
• It was formed in **January 1965**.
 
• It recommends the **minimum support prices (MSP)** and **issues prices for paddy and wheat.**
 
• It is a joint office of the ministry of agriculture & farmers welfare.
 
• It raises productivity and overall grain production in line with the emerging demand patterns in the country.
 
• It recommends MSPs of** 23 commodities**, are following:
 
 
• **7 oilseeds** including groundnut, rapeseed-mustard, soybean, sesamum, sunflower, safflower, and nigerseed.
 
• **7 kinds of cereal** including paddy, wheat, maize, sorghum, pearl millet, barley, and ragi.
 
• **5 pulses** including gram, tur, moong, urad, and lentil.
 
• **4 commercial crops** include copra, sugarcane, cotton, and raw jute.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Council of Agricultural Research**__

 __
 
• ICAR was **first reorganized in 1965.**
 
• The **Indian Council of Agricultural Research is an autonomous organization.**
 
• It is under the **Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India.**
 
• **Headquarters**- New Delhi.
 
• There is a total of **101 ICAR institutes and 71 agricultural universities **spread across the country.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**__
 
 
• **NITI Aayog **is **not a** constitutional body. 
 
• It was **established on January 1, 2015.**
 
• It is formed in place of the Planning Commission. o The** ex-officio Chairman of this is the Prime Minister.**
 
• It is the premier policy **Think Tank of the Government of India**, providing both directional and policy inputs.

questions.question: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress when India won its freedom in the year 1947?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**J. B. Kripalani.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **J. B. Kripalani**__

 __
 
• ​He was the** president of the Indian National Congress in 1947.**
 
• He was popularly known as **Acharya Kripalani.**
 
• From 1920 to 1927, he worked as the principal of **Gujarat Vidyapeeth which was an educational institution set up by Gandhi.** There he earned the **Epithet 'Acharya'.**
 
• He was elected the **General Secretary of the Indian National Congress (INC) in 1934 and continued to serve in the post for a long time till 1945.**
 
• In November** 1946**, he was elected the **President of the Congress Party.​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ​**Jawaharlal Nehru**__

 __
 
• ​He was the **first Prime minister of India.**
 
• He was also** India's longest-serving prime minister **(15 Aug 1947 to 27 May 1964)
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru along with Srinivasa Iyengar and Subhash Chandra Bose founded the Independence for India League in the year 1928 which put forth the demand for complete independence.
 
• **Books were written by him**: The Discovery of India, Letters from a Father to his Daughter, Glimpses of World History etc.
 
 
 
• **​Vallabhbhai Patel**__
 __
 
• ​He was popularly known as **Sardar Patel, Bismarck of India, Iron Man of India, Strong Man.**
 
• He was the **first Deputy Prime Minister of India.**
 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's statue or known as the Statue of Unity is situated in Gujarat India. It is the world's tallest statue standing at a height of 182 meters.
 
• Indian National Trade Union Congress was founded in 1947 by him.
 
• In 1928, he led the peasant movement in Bardoli, a taluka in Gujarat, against the enhancement of land revenue.
 
 
 
• ​**Abul Kalam Azad**__
 
 
• ​He was an **Indian independence activist, Islamic theologian, writer, and senior leader of the Indian National Congress.**
 
• **He was the First Education Minister in the Indian government.**
 
• He is commonly remembered as **Maulana Azad.**
 
• His contribution to establishing the education foundation in India is recognised by celebrating his birthday as National Education Day across India.

questions.question: In 711 CE, Arab general _______ conquered Sind, which became a part of the Caliph’s domain.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Bin Qasim.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **711 CE, Arab General Muhammad Qasim** conquered the Sind province.
 
• It was the **first Arab victory in India** and it led to the foundation for **Arab invasion in India.**
 
• He succeeded in conquering Sind in his third attempt in which he defeated Dahir, the King of Sind.
 
• **Muhammad Bin Qasim**__
 __
 
• He is also known as** Laquab of Imad-ad-Din.**
 
• He was born on **31st December, 695 AD.**
 
• He was the **first Muslim to invade** India and was the** commander of the Umayyad Caliphate.**
 
• He was sent as a prisoner to Mesopotamia.
 
• In 711 AD he defeated Raja Dahir.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Ghori**__

 __
 
• He was the third Muslim ruler who invaded India.
 
• His real name was Shahabuddin allas Muizudin Muhammad Ghori.
 
• He was defeated by Prithviraj in the First Battle of Tarain in 1191 AD and recovered Bhatinda.
 
• In the second battle of Tarain (1192AD) the joined forces of the Rajput rulers under Prithviraj were defeated by Muhammad Ghori. Prithviraj was held as a prisoner and later put to death.
 
• **Qutb-Ud-din Aibak** was appointed as the **commander by Muhammad of Ghori.**
 
 
 
• **Qutub-ud-din Aibak**__
 __
 
• ​He was the **first Sultan of Delhi in 1206 AD.**
 
• He was in charge of the **Ghurid territories and later became the ruler of the Delhi Sultanate** ruled by the **Mamluk Dynasty 1,1210.**
 
• He is known for commissioning the **Qutub Minar in Delhi.****​**
 
 
 
• **Muhammad-Bin-Tughlaq**__
 
 
• ​He was the **Sultan of Delhi from 1325 to 1351.**
 
• He was the **eldest son of Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq** the** founder of the Tughlaq dynasty.**
 
• In 1327, he** shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatbad** in the **Deccan, in present-day Maharashtra**.

questions.question: A message that tries to trick a person into providing information such as his social security number, bank account information or login username and password for a website is a type of cyber attack called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phishing.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phishing:**__

 __
 
• Phishing is the **attempt to acquire sensitive information such as usernames, passwords, and credit card details (and sometimes, indirectly, money), often for malicious reasons, by masquerading as a trustworthy entity in an electronic communication.**
 
• The first recorded use of the term** "phishing"** was in the cracking toolkit **AOHell created by Koceilah Rekouche in 1995.**
 
• **Types of phishing**:
 
 
• Email phishing
 
• Spear pishing
 
• Whaling and CEO Fraud
 
• Clone phishing
 
• Voice phishing SMS phishing
 
• Calendar phishing
 
• Page hijacking.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Macro Virus**__

 __
 
• **A macro virus **is a piece of malicious code written in the same macro language used in everyday applications, such as Microsoft Word, Excel, and Powerpoint.
 
• The attack code commonly hides in documents and spreadsheets and is activated as soon as you open the file.
 
• Once the macro virus has infected one of your applications, it triggers malware designed to cause damage to your computer and further spread the virus.
 
• Since the code runs on software and not on operating systems, it can infect any computer, even your Mac.
 
 
 
• **Zombie**__
 __
 
• **A Zombie** is a fictional character that can replicate itself.
 
 
 
• **Worm**__
 
 
• **A computer worm is a malicious program that replicates itself in order to spread to other computers.**

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest river island in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Majuli Island.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Majuli Island:**__

 __
 
• Majuli is the **largest inhabited riverine island in the world located in the Brahmaputra River.**
 
• It is India's **first Island district consisting of nearly 144 villages with a population of approximately 1.6 lakh.**
 
• It is a centre of Neo Vaishnavite culture initiated by Saint reformer Srimanta Sankardev in the 15th century.
 
• It has nearly** 65 Sattras** which is a religious and cultural institution.
 
• It is surrounded by the Subhasini river in the north, Brahmaputra river in the south, and Kherkutia islands in the northeast.
 
• It is mostly inhabited by the 'Mishing tribe'.
 
• Mishing, Assamese, and Deori are popular languages used on this Island.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gundu Island**__

 __
 
• Gundu is the **smallest island around Kochi with an area of 5 acres.**
 
• It is surrounded by coconut trees.
 
• It can be reached from Vypin island only by boat.
 
 
 
• **Divar Island**__
 __
 
• The Divar Island lies in the Mandovi river in the Indian state of Goa.
 
• It is located approx upriver 10 km from Panjim.
 
 
 
• **Diu Island **__
 
 
• It is an island off the southern coast of Gujarat's Kathiawar peninsula.
 
• The island lies 5 km to the east of Diu Head.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is called the month of merits and is celebrated between May and June?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saga Dawa.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saga Dawa:**__

 __
 
• **Saga Dawa is celebrated to mark the birth, enlightenment, and attainment of Nirvana of Gautam Buddha**.
 
• Buddha Jayanti in the **Bhutia language is called Saga Dawa.**
 
• The period for celebrating it was officially decided only in 1950, and since then, the festival has been celebrated on an annual basis.
 
• The highlight of the festival is giving alms to the needy; a virtue practiced throughout the month, conforming to the message of Buddha's life.
 
• Masks play an important role in Saga Dawa.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Bhanu Jayanti**
 
 
 
• It is celebrated in the state to commemorate the birth anniversary of Bhanubhakta Acharya Adikavi
 
 
 
 

 **Lossong**
 
 
 
• It is the most popular festival in Sikkim.
 
• It is usually celebrated at the end of the tenth Tibetan lunar month (usually December).
 
• It is the most important festival among the Bhutias in India and is marked by traditional Chaan dancing and merrymaking.
 
 
 
 

 **Losar**
 
 
 
• It is celebrated in the Ladakh region.
 
• The festival is celebrated on the 1st day of the eleventh month of the Tibetan Calendar.

questions.question: A mass of snow and ice that moves slowly under the influence of gravity along a confined course away from its place of accumulation is called a _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Glacier.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The moving ice mass** downslope under the impact of gravity is called a glacier.**
 
• **About 10% of the earth's surface is now covered by the glacier.**
 
• Glacier is formed due to the accumulation of ice above snow-line under extreme cold climate.
 
• Glaciers begin forming in places where more snow piles up each year than melts. Soon after falling, the snow begins to compress or become denser and tightly packed.
 
• The process of snow compacting into glacial firn (dense, grainy ice) is called firnification.
 
• Different parts of a glacier move at different speeds. The flowing ice in the middle of the glacier moves faster than the base.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Plateau**__

 __
 
• A plateau is a** flat-topped tableland.**
 
• Plateaus occur in every continent and take up a third of the Earth's land.
 
• They are one of the four major landforms, along with mountains, plains, and hills.
 
• Plateaus, like mountains, may be young or old. The Deccan plateau in India is one of the oldest plateaus.
 
 
 
• **Lagoon**__
 __
 
• ​**A lagoon is a body of water separated from larger bodies of water by a natural barrier.**
 
• There are two types of lagoons: Atoll and coastal.
 
 
 
• **Block Mountain**__
 
 
• **Block mountains are formed due to the upward movement of the middle block between two normal faults.**
 
• The upthrown block is also called a horst.
 
• Block mountains are generally formed in high plateaux or broad domes.

questions.question: ISRO launched ______, it’s 42nd communication satellite, in December 2020.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CMS-01.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **CMS-01:**__

 __
 
• **CMS-01** is the name of the satellite launched by **ISRO using its PSLV-C50 rocket.**
 
• **ISRO** launched a communication satellite CMS-01 which was formerly named **GSAT-12R** using its Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle rocket's XL variant numbered **PSLV-C50** from the second launch pad at the rocket port Sriharikota.
 
• **CMS-01** is a communication satellite that will provide services in the Extended-C Band of the frequency spectrum, which would include the Indian mainland, Andaman and Nicobar, and Lakshadweep Islands.
 
• This is the **42nd communication satellite of India **and it is expected to have a mission life of seven years.
 
• PSLV-C50 ejected CMS-01 Into geosynchronous transfer orbit after 20 minutes into its flight and the satellite was taken up from there and positioned at geosynchronous stationary orbit.
 
• The **CMS-01** is a replacement for** GSAT-12** that was launched in **2011** with a mission life of eight years.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Formation**: 15 August 1969 
 
• **Headquarters**: Bengaluru

questions.question: From which of the following sources does the brain get energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Glucose.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Glucose:**__

 __
 
• Glucose is a** form of sugar.**
 
• It is the primary source of energy for every cell in the body.
 
• Because the brain is** so rich in nerve cells, or neurons it is the most energy-demanding organ, using one-half of all the sugar energy in the body.**
 
• Brain functions such as thinking, memory, and learning are closely linked to glucose levels and how efficiently the brain uses this fuel source.
 
• The effects of glucose and other forms of sugar on the brain may be the most profound in diabetes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fatty acids:**__

 __
 
• Fatty acids are the **building blocks of the fat in our bodies and in the food we eat.**
 
• During digestion, the body breaks down fats into fatty acids, which can then be absorbed into the blood.
 
• Fatty acid molecules are usually joined together in groups of three, forming a molecule called a triglyceride.
 
 
 
• **Amino acids:**__
 __
 
• Amino acids are **molecules that combine to form proteins.**
 
• It is the building block of life.
 
• The human body uses amino acids to make proteins to help the body break down food, grow, repair body tissue, perform many other body functions.
 
 
 
• **Nucleic acids:**__
 
 
• Nucleic acids are **naturally occurring chemical compounds that serve as the primary information-carrying molecules in cells.**
 
• **They play an important role in directing protein synthesis.**
 
• The two main classes of nucleic acids are deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ribonucleic acid (RNA).

questions.question: With which of the following musical instruments is the musician Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Santoor.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Shiv Sharma:**__** **

 __
 
• He is an **Indian Santoor virtuoso** who is credited with shifting the instrument from a predominantly accompaniment and ensemble role in the Sufi music of Kashmir to a solo role in the Hindustani classical music tradition of North India.
 
• He was born on **January 13, 1938, in Jammu and Kashmir India.**
 
• He has single-handedly lifted his folk instrument the Santoor to full acceptance within the classical solo field.
 
 
 
• **Santoor**__
 
 
• It is a** trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer **and a variation of the Iranian Santoor.
 
• It is generally made of walnut and has** 25 bridges.**
 
• Each bridge has **4 strings, making for a total of 100 strings.**
 
• It is a traditional** instrument in Jammu and Kashmir.**

questions.question: What is the molecular formula for hydrochloric acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**HCl.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **molecular formula for hydrochloric acid** is** HCl.**
 
• **Properties of Hydrochloric Acid:**__
 __
 
• Strongly acidic
 
• Viscous and colourless
 
• Highly corrosive acid
 
• Pungent smell
 
• Properties dependent upon concentration - Melting and boiling point, pH, and density
 
 
 
• **Uses of HCl:**__
 
 
• Used in rubber and textile industries.
 
• Production of chlorides, fertilizers, dye, and organic compounds Refining of metals.
 
• Regulate pH of solutions.
 
• Unblock pores in oil wells.
